title: Canonical rank-one comparison for intrinsic pro-etale constant modules
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] and a finite commutative ring $A$, use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and its constant commutative ring sheaf $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $M_X=A_X$ as its own ordinary module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], using Mathlib's rank-one module, and $C_X$ for the constant fixed-scalar sheaf of the rank-one $A$-module. Let $E_X$ be the canonical intrinsic coefficient realization used in [def-weil-extension-by-zero], obtained by module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] along the constant-scalar unit; use its scalar-unit section map from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Define $c_X:E_X(C_X)\simeq M_X$ to be the unique module-sheaf isomorphism whose component sends the realization of every constant section $a\in A$ on every site object to the same scalar section of $A_X$. Such a unique isomorphism exists: both successive sheafifications have the same underlying associated abelian sheaf and the same constant scalar action. This defines the canonical rank-one comparison, including for the zero ring and the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; algebraic structures transported through sheafification as in sites.tex Tag 00YV; applied twice to the constant rank-one module.

proof.text: Restrict the intrinsic coefficient-ring unit module along the constant-scalar unit. Its underlying abelian presheaf is already a sheaf, so this gives a sheaf of fixed-scalar modules. The constant-scalar unit is a natural linear map into this sheaf. Extend it through fixed-scalar sheafification. The scalar unit is locally injective and locally surjective, as is the fixed-scalar sheafification unit. Cancellation of these properties shows that the extension is locally bijective, hence an isomorphism of sheaves.

Regard the fixed-scalar isomorphism as an isomorphism of module presheaves over the constant ring presheaf. Transpose it through the associated-module-sheaf adjunction. The transpose is an isomorphism because it is the composite of its sheafification and the adjunction counit, both isomorphisms. The adjunction unit identity and the fixed-scalar sheafification factorization prove the required normalization on every constant scalar section.

For uniqueness, transpose any other normalized comparison through the same adjunction. Its underlying fixed-scalar presheaf map agrees with the constructed extension after precomposition with the constant-presheaf sheafification unit, by the normalization. Sheafification extensionality makes the transposes equal; injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalence and extensionality of isomorphisms give equality of the comparisons. All constructions and identities hold for the zero ring and the empty scheme.
